security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, CSS snippets, placeholder URLs, and setup text. Confirmed risks are limited to reset commands that can terminate local processes and example servers binding to 0.0.0.0. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Reset examples use kill -9 through xargs.
remediation.suggestion: Use graceful shutdown steps first, avoid hiding errors, and require explicit user confirmation before terminating processes.
Default examples to 127.0.0.1 unless external interface binding is required for a documented tunnel setup.

remediation.issue: Environment file examples lack safety guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short warning to keep .env files out of source control and avoid logging secret values.

content.user_title: Build ChatGPT Apps With Interactive Widgets
content.value_statement: Building ChatGPT apps requires coordinated MCP server, widget, and metadata patterns. This skill gives practical templates and debugging guidance for working apps.
actual_capabilities: Explains ChatGPT app architecture with MCP tools and embedded widgets.
Provides FastMCP server templates for serving widget HTML resources.
Shows response metadata patterns for text/html+skybridge widgets.
Documents window.openai APIs for widget actions and tool output.
Gives debugging steps for ngrok tunnels, widget caching, and app registration.
limitations: It is guidance and templates, not a generated production application.
It focuses on development with ChatGPT Developer Mode and local tunnels.
It does not replace OpenAI platform documentation for policy or API changes.
Widget behavior still needs testing inside ChatGPT, not only a browser preview.

use_cases.title: Prototype a ChatGPT App
use_cases.description: Create a FastMCP server and widget structure for a first working app.

use_cases.title: Debug Widget Rendering
use_cases.description: Trace loading, metadata, MIME type, and cache issues when widgets do not appear.

use_cases.title: Standardize App Templates
use_cases.description: Use repeatable file structures and response metadata patterns across app projects.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter App
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a minimal ChatGPT app with one MCP tool and one widget.

prompt_templates.title: Add Widget Actions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design three widget buttons that send useful follow-up messages in ChatGPT.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot Rendering
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to diagnose why my ChatGPT widget stays on Loading and suggest checks in order.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my app architecture for metadata, resources, tunnel setup, and widget interaction risks.

output_examples.input: I need a basic ChatGPT app structure with one widget.
output_examples.output: A concise project outline with server files, widget resource responsibilities, and registration steps.

output_examples.input: My widget does not render in ChatGPT.
output_examples.output: A prioritized checklist covering server reachability, widget metadata, MIME type, app cache, and tunnel status.

output_examples.input: I want buttons that continue the conversation.
output_examples.output: A widget interaction plan using supported window.openai methods and simple action labels.

best_practices: Test widgets inside ChatGPT because browser previews cannot fully simulate window.openai.
Keep widget HTML, CSS, and JavaScript self-contained during early development.
Use fresh app registration when cache behavior hides recent widget changes.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on complex browser APIs that may fail in the ChatGPT iframe.
Do not omit response metadata for widgets that must render in ChatGPT.
Do not treat placeholder tunnel URLs as production deployment guidance.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build ChatGPT apps that combine MCP tools with embedded interactive widgets.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete production app?
faq.answer: No. It provides templates, patterns, and troubleshooting guidance for developers.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Why does it mention ngrok?
faq.answer: It uses ngrok as a local development tunnel so ChatGPT can reach an MCP server.

faq.question: Can I test widgets only in a browser?
faq.answer: No. Browser testing is useful, but ChatGPT provides the real window.openai environment.

faq.question: Is this only for standard MCP servers?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on ChatGPT apps with widgets, not plain MCP servers without UI.
